title: Tim Dooley / SPLC Prediction Audit — Pre-Indictment Claims, Later Allegations, and Recovery Targets
status: specialized prediction audit; one dated pre-event directional precursor recovered; direct SPLC-specific prediction still unresolved
purpose: Work backward from the April 21, 2026 federal criminal indictment of the Southern Poverty Law Center and test whether Tim Dooley made materially matching statements before the event. Separate genuine pre-event statements from public prior knowledge, post-event recollection, symbolic/systemic criticism and later assistant synthesis.
epistemic_rule: An indictment contains allegations, not proven facts. A Tim statement counts as prediction evidence only if its wording and timestamp can be established before the relevant later allegation became public. General criticism of SPLC, generic suspicion of hidden funding, or known FBI/SPLC relationships are not equivalent to predicting a criminal indictment.

anchor_events.event: In Estate of Donald A. King / Dustin Inman Society v. SPLC, the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Alabama granted SPLC summary judgment on all counts in a civil defamation dispute involving SPLC hate-group designations.
anchor_events.importance: This earlier civil case creates ambiguity whenever an early-2026 Tim conversation refers simply to 'the SPLC case.'

anchor_events.event: A federal grand jury indicted SPLC on 11 counts involving wire fraud, false statements to a federally insured bank and conspiracy to commit concealment money laundering.
anchor_events.allegations: DOJ alleged that from 2014-2023 SPLC secretly funneled more than $3 million in donated funds to individuals associated with violent extremist groups and used bank accounts tied to fictitious entities to conceal the nature, source, ownership and control of funds.

anchor_events.event: CBS reported that IRS-CI/FBI agents had investigated SPLC's paid-informant/shell-account structure in 2019-2020 for possible tax offenses but no tax charges resulted after IRS lawyers determined the program was legally structured for tax purposes.
anchor_events.importance: Important countercontext: some underlying informant/payment architecture predated 2026 and had been investigated, although CBS said the prior probe had not previously been reported. This does not resolve the later fraud/bank allegations.

anchor_events.event: A superseding indictment added factual allegations while retaining the core charges.
anchor_events.allegations: DOJ alleged approximately $4.1 million in tax-exempt funds were used to pay informants in extremist organizations, including allegations that some recruited members or purchased material connected with Klan activity.
anchor_events.boundary: SPLC denies fraud and argues its informant program was legitimate investigative work that prevented violence and supplied information to law enforcement.

anchor_events.event: A second superseding indictment added former SPLC executive Heidi Beirich as a defendant and additional charges/allegations.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: SPLC had long publicly operated Klanwatch/Intelligence Project and monitored extremist organizations.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: Predicting that SPLC had intelligence-gathering relationships with extremist milieus is low-surprise by itself.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: FBI Director Kash Patel publicly severed ties with SPLC on October 3, 2025.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: A generic 'SPLC has FBI ties' statement after that date is not hidden-information foresight.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: CBS reported in May 2026 that a 2019-2020 IRS-CI/FBI investigation had examined paid-informant shell accounts but produced no tax charges; CBS described the prior probe as previously unreported.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: If Tim independently named paid informants plus concealed bank structures before April 21, that would be more probative than merely knowing SPLC worked with law enforcement. But the archive has not yet recovered such a Tim source.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: The specific April allegations concerning fictitious bank entities, detailed payment channels and the charged fraud/money-laundering theory became public with the indictment.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: Any clearly timestamped Tim statement naming those mechanisms before April 21 would carry much higher evidentiary weight.

current_conclusion: There is now at least one defensible pre-event signal in the relevant mechanism family: on September 23, 2025, Tim publicly asked who was really the boss and funder behind 'all these extreme things,' about 210 days before the April 21 SPLC indictment later alleged concealed donor-funded payments to people associated with extremist groups. That is an interesting directional precursor, not a direct SPLC prediction. A March 31, 2026 smear/information/currency formulation is another thematic precursor but is even less specific. No direct pre-April public statement naming SPLC plus indictment, fraud, banks or paid informants has been recovered in the current corpus. The remembered February 18 'predicted the SPLC case' claim remains unverified and ambiguous. Accordingly the archive should say Tim showed early attention to hidden funding/extremism mechanisms, while the stronger claim that he predicted the SPLC criminal case remains an open source-recovery question.
